questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The ranking of the university, the culture being quite different from the one in Denmark and a new study environment.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: None

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy as NTU kept us informed and stayed in contact with us during the process.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had an NTU student partner who helped us during course registration so I would ask them questions about the process.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: none

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I stayed in a single dorm room close to campus

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There were no meal plans available but a convenience store right nearby and many food choices

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There is a 24/7 reception which is nice and a secure area. Its also very affordable.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We had to meet up and bring some forms and collect stamps. They announce the date and time via email

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There were booths during registration for different sections needed to be completed and there were people working behind each of them.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very mixed. There are more rounds so it's possible but be sure to have back up courses because you aren't prioritised as an exchange student for the spots available. I only got half of the classes I needed even after first and second round.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: What I mentioned above. Also, it is a good idea to apply for many subjects with forhåndsgodkendelse as the chances of getting the exact courses you initially wanted is slim as well as potential schedule clashes. NTU doesn't allow to be enrolled in courses that are at the same time and they will automatically remove you from one if this happens so apply for approvel for a lot of courses to make the course registration process less stressful.

questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Entrepreneurial Finance if you do economics or finance as this course is for international students and quite easy to follow along with how the work was distributed. It made it much easier to follow.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I am not sure I encountered unexpected costs. Keep in mind public transport doesn't run at night there so you might have to take taxis and uber.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Eating out was less expensive than expected for sure. The public transport is also quite chip; I remember if you use the student ID as metro card, it cost 12 NTD per way which is less than 3kr.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were many clubs especially in for sports. And a lot of facilities.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were cultural activities aligned with Taiwan and there was a 'Far from Home' activity picnic. Another one was visiting a village and learning of their culture along with tea ceremony. NTU also has a day where the different clubs showcase.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Definitely the sports; there are also many social activities which can be found on social medias like WhatsApp such as hiking. So I would recommend to keep an eye out on these. NTU also has a ceremic pottery club that my friend really enjoyed.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go and see as much as Taiwan as possible or go abroad as many did. Many went to Japan or South Korea during holidays.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It didn't take too long. In my experience, Taiwanese peoples english is quite decent so ordering coffee and food was not difficult. They are generally quiet on public transport but that came easy. The food was sometimes tough for me but thankfully they have a lot of different options as well as a lot of vegetarian food.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the groupchats on social media pre-arrival and see. I can also recommend living in a social place. My faculty had a mingling event where we get to meet and talk with each other as well. My dorm also had a welcome party with activities. Bars and clubs also had welcome parties. There are many opportunities to socialise so I wouldn't worry:)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The food and people staring were the toughest. As mentioned above, thankfully there are many different food options in Taiwan and when it comes to the staring... you get used it.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The nature and trips were my favourite part. I also did ICL so I got to go on two trips which was definitely a cultural experience.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Look for accomodation well in advance; many people were in between places as the semester started.
2. When applying for pre-approval, include a lot of courses just in case. The process takes time and you might not have that opportunity later, and with how NTU prioritises spots, there is a slim chance of getting all the courses you want.
3. Get an MRT (metro) card on your first day and ensure you always have NTD cash.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The most useful was what was written above. Download the Uber app, enroll in Chinese and ICL, have google translate in case. Have a couple of different payment cards in case one has issues.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: For me, it was definitely the friends I made. It's been over a month since I left and I still talk daily with my friends and we will be visiting each other. My exchange experience wouldn't have been as fulfilling if it wasn't for them.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The food and constantly eating out. If you stay in the NTU dorm, unless you get assigned a suite where there is a shared kitchen, you basically have to eat out and groceries arent super cheap in Taiwan. It's definitely cheaper to eat out but it gets tiring at some point.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No

questions.answer: Yes
